citations.narrative:
This is a search inspection.
The facility sold and exhibited exotic animals to the public for compensation without an active USDA license. The facility
had applied for a license with USDA APHIS Animal Care but failed to complete the Pre-license process and their
application was cancelled November 6, 2023. Between 1-March-2025 and 1-June-2026, the facility exhibited at least one
red kangaroo approximately eight times. Additionally, the facility sold two African crested porcupines and donated another
African crested porcupine.
Conducting regulated activity without a USDA license does not comply with the Animal Welfare Act or ensure that APHIS
officials can assess the care of the animals. The facility must obtain a license from the USDA to continue conducting
regulated activity under the Animal Welfare Act. Continuing to conduct regulated activity without a license is a serious
violation of the Animal Welfare Act.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
